name: Gamelan
description: The bronze orchestras of Java and Bali: metallophones, gong-chimes and hanging gongs in their own pelog and slendro tunings.
credit: Sounds put together for HO[LO] (CC0): HO[LO] Desk's built-in synths and effects, and Casa da Música's Virtual Gamelan by Digitópia, Casa da Música, Porto (Artistic License 2.0), Balinese gamelan by Akito van Troyer for the One Laptop per Child sound library (CC BY 3.0). Each pack keeps its own licence and credit.

source.note: No audio of its own: its sounds play the packs it requires and HO[LO] Desk’s built-in synths.

sounds.name: Saron, Pelog
sounds.note: Javanese saron in pelog: bronze keys struck with a mallet, carrying the melody.

sounds.name: Saron, Slendro
sounds.note: Javanese saron in slendro, the five-note tuning.

sounds.name: Bonang
sounds.note: Javanese bonang: small kettle gongs in rows, for interlocking figures.

sounds.name: Gendèr
sounds.note: Javanese gendèr: thin bronze keys over tube resonators, soft and ringing.

sounds.name: Gong Ageng
sounds.note: The great hanging gong that closes each cycle, with the smaller gong suwukan on the key above.

sounds.name: Kempul
sounds.note: Smaller hanging gongs that mark the cycle within.

sounds.name: Gangsa
sounds.note: Balinese gangsa: bright metallophones for fast interlocking figures.

sounds.name: Reyong
sounds.note: Balinese reyong: a row of small gongs played by several players at once.
